summary: The PIR motion sensor video is the clear winner, with about 1,900 combined views and most of the likes, shares and saves, mostly from Instagram. Every other video is tiny, with under 200 views each, so the channel is very new and most topics have not caught on yet. The English Arduino video got views only on YouTube and was never posted to Instagram, so there is not enough data to say whether English works.
winningPattern: Hindi explainer about a sensor people meet in daily life (PIR motion sensor), with a myth-busting or surprising-claim hook ('Aapko Dekhta Nahi!') followed by a 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' question, a 🤔 emoji and #shorts. It works best on Instagram, which gave about 2.7x the views of YouTube on that video.
doMore: Open with a surprising or 'you are wrong' claim about a sensor people use every day, then explain it in the same video
Post every Hindi video to Instagram first and treat it as the main platform, then cross-post to YouTube
Pick single-sensor topics (IR, ultrasonic, LDR, buzzer, relay) that people can picture instantly
End each video with a clear prompt to save or share, such as 'Dost ko bhejo jise ye nahi pata'
Test the PIR title and hook structure again on two or three new topics before changing the format
stopDoing: Plain 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' titles with no surprising claim, like the phone orientation and mall door videos
Posting English videos to YouTube only, since this gives no comparison with Hindi
Drawing big conclusions from videos with under 150 views
